raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On MI35x, `moe_sorting_small` replaces aiter's MoE sorting at small batches. It can also emit the stage-1 MXFP8 activation quant in the same launch, which saves aiter's separate `fused_mx_quant_moe_sort` launch. Two gates kept DeepSeek-V4.1 off both paths:

- **The quant gate required `hidden % 2048 == 0`.** DeepSeek-V4.1's hidden size is 5120, so every MoE layer still ran aiter's stage-1 quant as its own launch.
- **The distributed sort only ran up to 256 experts.** With `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`, V4.1's target MoE has E=385 (384 routed + shared). Rows 10-16 at top-7 therefore went to aiter's sort plus quant, two launches.

At TP4 batch 1-2, a decode cycle runs about 43 MoE layers. Each launch costs about 2-4 us under graph replay.

## Modifications

All changes are in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_sorting_small.py`.

- **Stage-1 quant at 1024- or 2048-column steps.** The quant is now emitted whenever the hidden size is a multiple of 1024: 5120 (V4.1) and 7168 (V3) gain it, and 2048-multiples keep their existing step. Smaller steps stay on aiter; they were never checked bitwise or timed, and they would unroll many quant iterations per pair.
- **Distributed sort up to E=385, up to 112 routing pairs.** The limit is the named constant `_DISTRIBUTED_MAX_PAIRS_UP_TO_385_EXPERTS`. Past 112 pairs the distributed sort + quant loses to aiter at E=385 (it breaks even near 126 and is slower from 140).

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/amd/test_moe_sorting_small.py` (gfx950): 7 passed. Each case guards one regression:

- **Sort parity at E=385, 16 rows (112 pairs, block 32/64).** This is the first time the distributed sort runs with more than 256 experts.
- **Quant bytes and e8m0 scales at hidden 5120**, checked bitwise against aiter's `fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort`, for 9 rows (compact sort) and 16 rows (distributed sort).
- **The 16/17-row cutoff (112/119 pairs).** Fails if the E≤385 clause is dropped or widened.
- **End to end, `fused_moe` A8W4 at hidden 5120 / inter 640.**
  - Covers 385/7 at 1 and 16 rows, routed through the HIP split-K router GEMV and gate, plus the DSpark draft's 129/4 at 1 row.
  - The stage-1 GEMM output must be bitwise equal to stock aiter's.
  - The test also fails if the sort-time quant was skipped; restoring the old `% 2048` gate makes it fail.
  - The full MoE output is checked within 2% of its max only, because stage 2 accumulates top-k rows with bf16 atomics.

End to end, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 with DSpark and real acceptance, together with #43821, on main 166b4ae7fc (unit tests re-run after rebasing on f006fb49ec): correct answers (391 / Paris / 42), 0 NaN / error lines, real accept length 2.54 against about 2.55 on main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Whole MoE layer** (`do_bench_cudagraph`, gfx950, hidden 5120, inter 640, A8W4). Time in µs, old → new; launches per layer go 5 → 4 where the quant is fused.

| E / top-k | 1 row | 2 | 5 | 10 | 16 | 40 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 385 / 7 | 25.7 → 23.3 | 30.1 → 26.7 | 44.5 → 42.3 | 84.0 → 75.2 | 100.3 → 90.2 | unchanged |
| 129 / 4 | 24.1 → 21.5 | 26.5 → 23.6 | 31.0 → 28.3 | 44.9 → 41.9 | 54.0 → 51.2 | 100.6 → 96.2 |

**Sort alone** (`do_bench_cudagraph`), aiter → this PR:

| E / top-k | rows (pairs) | aiter | this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 385 / 7 | 8 / 10 / 12 (56 / 70 / 84) | 11.8 / 15.0 / 15.6 µs | 4.1 / 10.0 / 10.1 µs |
| 257 / 9 (V3 with fused shared expert) | 8 / 10 / 12 (72 / 90 / 108) | 10.1 / 12.7 / 13.3 µs | 9.2 / 9.2 / 9.3 µs |

The cutoff covers every E from 257 to 385 and was measured at both ends.

Per-step decode throughput, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 on MI350X, published MI355X c8 arguments, AgentX simulated acceptance 3.51. Median and [min–max] over 3 interleaved rounds; each round boots every arm once:

| running requests | main | this PR | this PR + #43821 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 459 [457–463] | **465 [464–466], +1.3%** | **475 [473–476], +3.6%** |
| 4 | 1,370 [1,366–1,398] | 1,382 [1,379–1,382], +0.8% (within noise) | 1,398 [1,383–1,398], +2.0% (within noise) |
| 8 | 2,304 [2,303–2,367] | 2,355 [2,320–2,356], +2.2% (within noise) | 2,352 [2,338–2,403], +2.1% (within noise) |

Each cell is the median over the 3 rounds of each round's median per-step `gen throughput`, with the [min–max] of the round medians. A change counts as real only when every round of the arm beats every round of main. At 1 running request it does, with a small margin; at 4-8 the differences stay inside main's own round-to-round spread.

Not executed: speed at hidden 7168 (V3) end to end. The 7168 quant uses the same 1024-column step that the 5120 test checks bitwise.

nodes.body:
Hi @kevin-mii, thanks for this PR. It overlaps a lot with #42498 (open since Oct 4), so I want to flag it before we both spend more time on the same change.

**Where it overlaps.** Every change this PR makes in `moe_sorting_small.py` is on lines that #42498 also changes:

- Quant step: `_mx_quant_chunk()` (2048 or 1024 columns) gives the same step as `qchunk = math.gcd(n_cols, 2048)` in #42498, for every hidden size that is a multiple of 1024.
- Emit gate in `apply_aiter_small_moe_sort_patch()`: `_mx_quant_chunk(hidden) is not None` here, `hidden % 1024 == 0` in #42498.
- `QCHUNK` and `num_quant` in both launches of `_run_small_sort()`.
- `_small_sort_supported()`: here the distributed sort runs up to 112 pairs at E ≤ 385. In #42498, more than 32 pairs at E < 512 go to the histogram + bitonic sort from #41900 (same change as #44004), and #42498 adds the quant to that kernel.

The tests overlap too: #42498 checks the quant bytes and scales bitwise against aiter at hidden 5120 and E=385 top-7 (9, 10 and 36 rows), and the 36/37-row cutoff. Merging both PRs gives 4 conflicts in the kernel file and 2 in the test file.

**How much.** For DeepSeek-V4.1 decode (E=385, top-7, hidden 5120), this PR fuses the quant at 1–16 rows and #42498 at 1–36 rows. So all of this PR's range is already covered by #42498, and it is about 44% of the #42498 range. On speed, your table shows 10.0–10.1 µs for the sort at 10–12 rows, and #42498 measured 4.5–5.4 µs for sort plus quant at 10–36 rows. The setups differ, so this is only a rough comparison, but it points to the bitonic path from 10 rows up.

**What is new here.** The end-to-end `fused_moe` test (target MoE 385/7 at 1 and 16 rows through the router, and the draft MoE 129/4) is not in #42498, and it is a good test to have.

**Suggestion.** Could you rebase this PR on #42498 and keep the new parts, mainly the end-to-end test? If you prefer, I can add the test to #42498 with credit to you. Note that #44009 already builds on #42498.

To avoid this in the future, could we both check the open PRs on the same file before starting new work? I will do the same. Happy to discuss.

             tl.store(qscale_ptr + sw, exp.to(tl.uint8))
 
 
+def _mx_quant_chunk(n_cols: int):
+    """Widest verified quant step (2048 or 1024) dividing `n_cols`; None skips the fused quant."""
+    for chunk in (2048, 1024):
+        if n_cols % chunk == 0:
+            return chunk
+    return None
+

+# measured at DeepSeek-V4's E=385 top-7: past it the distributed sort + quant loses to aiter
+_DISTRIBUTED_MAX_PAIRS_UP_TO_385_EXPERTS = 112

+    def _valid_scale_bytes(self, scale, sorted_ids, num_valid, m, n_cols):
+        """The e8m0 bytes of every real sorted row, at aiter's mx_scale_shuffle_idx address."""
+        n = int(num_valid[0])
+        rows = torch.arange(n, device=self.dev)
+        rows = rows[(sorted_ids[:n] & 0xFFFFFF) < m]
+        scalen_pad = ((n_cols // 32 + 7) // 8) * 8
+        y = torch.arange(n_cols // 32, device=self.dev)
+        base = (rows // 32) * (scalen_pad * 32) + (rows % 16) * 4 + (rows % 32) // 16
+        addr = base[:, None] + (y // 8) * 256 + (y % 4) * 64 + ((y % 8) // 4) * 2
+        return scale.view(torch.uint8).flatten()[addr]
+
+    def test_fused_mxfp8_quant_matches_aiter_dsv4_hidden(self):
+        """A hidden size off a 2048 multiple must still quantize each row and real-row scale
+        bitwise like aiter's `fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort`."""
+        bs, dim, E, topk = 32, 5120, 385, 7
+        # the widest compact sort (63 pairs) and the distributed one at the 112-pair cutoff
+        for m in (9, 16):
+            ids, w = self._routing(m, m, E, topk)
+            x = torch.randn(m, dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=self.dev)
+            x[:, :64] *= 1e-3  # spread the per-group scales
+            tok = self.S._pending_quant_input.set(x)
+            etok = self.S._emitted_quant.set(None)
+            try:
+                sid, sw, _, nv, _ = self.fm._moe_sorting_impl(
+                    ids, w, E, dim, torch.bfloat16, bs, None, None, 0, True
+                )
+                emitted = self.S._emitted_quant.get()
+            finally:
+                self.S._emitted_quant.reset(etok)
+                self.S._pending_quant_input.reset(tok)
+            msg = f"m={m}"
+            self.assertIsNotNone(emitted, msg)
+            ref_q, ref_s = self.orig_quant(
+                x,
+                sorted_ids=sid,
+                num_valid_ids=nv,
+                token_num=m,
+                topk=topk,
+                block_size=bs,
+                sorted_weights=sw,
+                num_experts_upper_bound=E,
+            )
+            self.assertTrue(
+                torch.equal(ref_q.view(torch.uint8), emitted[0].view(torch.uint8)),
+                msg,
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(ref_s.shape, emitted[1].shape, msg)
+            self.assertTrue(
+                torch.equal(
+                    self._valid_scale_bytes(ref_s, sid, nv, m, dim),
+                    self._valid_scale_bytes(emitted[1], sid, nv, m, dim),
+                ),
+                msg,
+            )
+
     def test_falls_back_to_aiter_past_compact_at_513_experts(self):
         m = 6
         ids, _ = self._routing(m, m)
         self.assertFalse(self.S._small_sort_supported(ids, 32, None, None, self.E))
 
+    def test_falls_back_to_aiter_past_112_pairs_at_385_experts(self):
+        """Past 112 pairs at E=385 the distributed sort is slower than aiter's."""
+        for m, small in ((16, True), (17, False)):
+            ids, _ = self._routing(m, m, 385, 7)
+            self.assertEqual(
+                self.S._small_sort_supported(ids, 32, None, None, 385), small, m
+            )
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(_gfx950(), "gfx950 (MI35x) only")
+class TestDsv4MoePrologue(CustomTestCase):
+    """The sort-time quant must hand DeepSeek-V4.1's decode stage1 GEMM (TP4 afp8_wfp4)
+    operands bitwise equal to stock aiter's."""
+
+    H, INTER = 5120, 640
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        import aiter.fused_moe as fm
+
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.moe import moe_sorting_small as S
+
+        S.apply_aiter_small_moe_sort_patch()
+        cls.S, cls.fm = S, fm
+        cls.dev = torch.device("cuda", 0)
+        cls._bound = os.environ.get("AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND")
+        # V4.1 serves with fp8 activations at every row count
+        os.environ["AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND"] = "0"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def tearDownClass(cls):
+        if cls._bound is None:
+            os.environ.pop("AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND", None)
+        else:
+            os.environ["AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND"] = cls._bound
+
+    def _experts(self, E, gen):
+        from aiter import dtypes
+        from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_scale
+
+        H, I = self.H, self.INTER
+
+        def fp4(*shape):
+            w = torch.randint(0, 256, shape, dtype=torch.uint8, generator=gen)
+            w = w.to(self.dev).view(dtypes.fp4x2)
+            w.is_shuffled = True
+            return w
+
+        def e8m0(rows, cols, gate_up):
+            s = torch.randint(118, 124, (rows, cols), dtype=torch.uint8, generator=gen)
+            return shuffle_scale(
+                s.to(self.dev).view(dtypes.fp8_e8m0), E, False, gate_up
+            )
+
+        return (
+            fp4(E, 2 * I, H // 2),
+            fp4(E, H, I // 2),
+            e8m0(E * 2 * I, H // 32, True),
+            e8m0(E * H, I // 32, False),
+        )
+
+    def _fused_moe(self, x, experts, weights, ids, stock):
+        """fused_moe output, the stage1 output the stage2 quant reads, and whether the
+        stage1 quant came from the sort."""
+        from aiter import ActivationType, QuantType
+        from aiter.ops.flydsl.moe_common import GateMode
+
+        fm, S = self.fm, self.S
+        w1, w2, w1_scale, w2_scale = experts
+        stage1_out, sort_time_quant = [], []
+        patched_quant = fm.fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort
+        patched_supported = S._small_sort_supported
+
+        def recording_quant(input, *args, **kwargs):
+            if input.shape[-1] == self.INTER:
+                stage1_out.append(input.clone())
+            else:
+                sort_time_quant.append(S._emitted_quant.get() is not None)
+            return patched_quant(input, *args, **kwargs)
+
+        fm.fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort = recording_quant
+        if stock:
+            S._small_sort_supported = lambda *args: False
+        try:
+            run = fm.fused_moe.__wrapped__ if stock else fm.fused_moe
+            out = run(
+                x,
+                w1,
+                w2,
+                weights,
+                ids,
+                quant_type=QuantType.per_1x32,
+                activation=ActivationType.Silu,
+                w1_scale=w1_scale,
+                w2_scale=w2_scale,
+                swiglu_limit=10.0,
+                gate_mode=GateMode.INTERLEAVE.value,
+            )
+        finally:
+            fm.fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort = patched_quant
+            S._small_sort_supported = patched_supported
+        self.assertEqual(len(stage1_out), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(len(sort_time_quant), 1)
+        return out, stage1_out[0], sort_time_quant[0]
+
+    def _route(self, x, gate_w, bias):
+        """V4.1's decode router: split-K GEMV + sqrtsoftplus gate + the shared slot."""
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.router_gemv_hip import rocm_router_gemv_split_k
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.rocm_router_gate import rocm_router_gate
+
+        logits = torch.empty(x.shape[0], gate_w.shape[0], device=self.dev)
+        partials = rocm_router_gemv_split_k(x, gate_w)
+        return rocm_router_gate(
+            logits, bias, 6, True, 1.5, partials=partials, num_shared=1
+        )
+
+    def test_target_moe_385_experts_top7(self):
+        E, topk = 385, 7
+        gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(E)
+        experts = self._experts(E, gen)
+        gate_w = (torch.randn(E - 1, self.H, generator=gen) * 0.02).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        gate_w = gate_w.to(self.dev)
+        bias = (torch.randn(E - 1, generator=gen) * 0.5).to(torch.bfloat16).to(self.dev)
+        # compact sort, and the distributed sort at the 112-pair cutoff
+        for m in (1, 16):
+            msg = f"M={m}"
+            x = torch.randn(m, self.H, generator=gen).to(torch.bfloat16).to(self.dev)
+            weights, ids = self._route(x, gate_w, bias)
+            self.assertEqual(ids.shape, (m, topk), msg)
+            ref_out, ref_stage1, _ = self._fused_moe(
+                x, experts, weights, ids, stock=True
+            )
+            out, stage1, fused = self._fused_moe(x, experts, weights, ids, stock=False)
+            self.assertTrue(fused, msg)
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(stage1, ref_stage1), msg)
+            # bf16 atomics round partial sums of up to topk rows: a few ulp of the row scale
+            err = (out.float() - ref_out.float()).abs().max().item()
+            self.assertLessEqual(err, 2e-2 * ref_out.float().abs().max().item(), msg)
+
+    def test_draft_moe_129_experts_top4(self):
+        """The draft MoE's sort-time quant must hand stage1 what stock aiter builds."""
+        E, topk, m = 129, 4, 1
+        gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(E)
+        experts = self._experts(E, gen)
+        x = torch.randn(m, self.H, generator=gen).to(torch.bfloat16).to(self.dev)
+        ids = torch.cat(
+            [torch.randperm(E - 1, generator=gen)[: topk - 1], torch.tensor([E - 1])]
+        )
+        ids = ids.view(m, topk).to(torch.int32).to(self.dev).contiguous()
+        weights = torch.rand(m, topk, generator=gen).to(self.dev)
+        ref_out, ref_stage1, _ = self._fused_moe(x, experts, weights, ids, stock=True)
+        out, stage1, fused = self._fused_moe(x, experts, weights, ids, stock=False)
+        self.assertTrue(fused)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(stage1, ref_stage1))
+        err = (out.float() - ref_out.float()).abs().max().item()
+        self.assertLessEqual(err, 2e-2 * ref_out.float().abs().max().item())
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()

issue_comments.body:
Hi @kevin-mii, thanks for this PR. It overlaps a lot with #42498 (open since Oct 4), so I want to flag it before we both spend more time on the same change.

**Where it overlaps.** Every change this PR makes in `moe_sorting_small.py` is on lines that #42498 also changes:

- Quant step: `_mx_quant_chunk()` (2048 or 1024 columns) gives the same step as `qchunk = math.gcd(n_cols, 2048)` in #42498, for every hidden size that is a multiple of 1024.
- Emit gate in `apply_aiter_small_moe_sort_patch()`: `_mx_quant_chunk(hidden) is not None` here, `hidden % 1024 == 0` in #42498.
- `QCHUNK` and `num_quant` in both launches of `_run_small_sort()`.
- `_small_sort_supported()`: here the distributed sort runs up to 112 pairs at E ≤ 385. In #42498, more than 32 pairs at E < 512 go to the histogram + bitonic sort from #41900 (same change as #44004), and #42498 adds the quant to that kernel.

The tests overlap too: #42498 checks the quant bytes and scales bitwise against aiter at hidden 5120 and E=385 top-7 (9, 10 and 36 rows), and the 36/37-row cutoff. Merging both PRs gives 4 conflicts in the kernel file and 2 in the test file.

**How much.** For DeepSeek-V4.1 decode (E=385, top-7, hidden 5120), this PR fuses the quant at 1–16 rows and #42498 at 1–36 rows. So all of this PR's range is already covered by #42498, and it is about 44% of the #42498 range. On speed, your table shows 10.0–10.1 µs for the sort at 10–12 rows, and #42498 measured 4.5–5.4 µs for sort plus quant at 10–36 rows. The setups differ, so this is only a rough comparison, but it points to the bitonic path from 10 rows up.

**What is new here.** The end-to-end `fused_moe` test (target MoE 385/7 at 1 and 16 rows through the router, and the draft MoE 129/4) is not in #42498, and it is a good test to have.

**Suggestion.** Could you rebase this PR on #42498 and keep the new parts, mainly the end-to-end test? If you prefer, I can add the test to #42498 with credit to you. Note that #44009 already builds on #42498.

To avoid this in the future, could we both check the open PRs on the same file before starting new work? I will do the same. Happy to discuss.
